land.text: Tabaristan, where Hasan ibn Zayd was 'recognized as emir by a part of the local population' in 864

predecessors.note: The Alid page's infobox names the Rashidun Caliphate as predecessor, which is not a territorial predecessor; the Tahirid dossier records Tabaristan as lost to the Zaydis in 864.

land.text: Tabaristan and Rayy, conquered by the Samanid general Asfar ibn Shiruya in 928

successors.note: Nasr II page: 'In 928, Asfar ibn Shiruya, a Dailamite military leader who now served the Samanids, conquered Tabaristan and Ray.' Gurgan went to the Samanids too.

land.text: Tabaristan and Gurgan, taken by Mardavij after Asfar's fall (the Alid page lists the Ziyarids among the successors)

successors.note: The Ziyarid dossier dates Mardavij's gain of Tabaristan to 932; the Zaydi state itself ended in 928.

capitals.name: Amol
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Amol', capital-in-exile Sari and Astarabad; the Samanids held Amol 900-913.

rulers.name: Muhammad ibn Zayd
rulers.note: Reign '6 January 884 - 3 October 900'; a usurper held Amul until October 884; killed after the Gurgan battle against the Samanids.

rulers.name: Hasan ibn Ali al-Utrush (al-Nasir li'l-Haqq)
rulers.note: Reign 'January 914 - January/February 917'; the Samanids held Tabaristan 900-913.

rulers.name: Hasan ibn al-Qasim (al-Da'i ila'l-Haqq)
rulers.note: Deposed briefly in 919 and in 923-926 by al-Utrush's sons (the Nasiris); last ruler (infobox '927-928').

correction.text: unchanged, holding from 864 (founding year) rather than 866

keyframe_review.note: 45.4 thousand km2 around Tabaristan and Gilan. The page: 'The first and most powerful Zaydi emirate was established in Tabaristan in 864'; Hasan ibn Zayd was chased out in 865 by Sulayman ibn Abdallah and from 867 'usually controlled Gurgan'. Shape unchanged; it should hold from 864 (with Tabaristan lost in 865 and recovered by 866-867).

46.1 thousand km2, the Cliopatria maximum. Hasan's base in Tabaristan with temporary control of Rayy (864-865, 867, 870, 872), Qazvin (865-868) and Qumis (873-879) and usually Gurgan from 867; Ya'qub's 874 invasion beat the Zaydid forces at Sari but withdrew. The page gives no area; no comparison possible.

40.6 thousand km2: the Tabaristan core after Gurgan is lost ('expelled from Gurgan by the Tahirid general Ishaq al-Sari in spring 877') and Hasan dies in 884. Muhammad ibn Zayd takes Amul in October 884.

correction.text: unchanged for 886-888; 889 to June 893 'most of his domains' occupied by Rafi' ibn Harthama (see the ledger)

keyframe_review.note: Right for 886-888. The page says 'the invasion of Rafi' ibn Harthama in 889-892, which occupied most of his domains' ('conquered most of them' in 888 or 889) and that Muhammad re-entered Amul on 24 June 893: the shape is mostly Rafi's from 889 to 893, and the Cliopatria gap 892-895 is the wrong way round (Zaydi absent 889-June 893, present 893-895).

correction.text: the 896-897 shape: Tabaristan and the Gilan edge, Muhammad back in Amul from 24 June 893

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe filling Cliopatria's gap 892-895: Muhammad is back in Amul from 24 June 893 and the Zaydid domain is the 896-897 shape (Gurgan recovered only after Rafi's death, c. 896).
40.9 thousand km2. 'Rafi' was killed shortly after by his rivals the Saffarids, whereupon Muhammad recovered Gurgan as well' (the Amr page has Rafi killed in Khwarazm in 896).

correction.text: unchanged for 898-900; 901-913 no Zaydi territory: the Samanids hold Tabaristan, the Alids in exile in Daylam

keyframe_review.note: Right for 898-900: Muhammad's reign ends 3 October 900 ('The Samanids prevailed, and the severely wounded Muhammad was captured') and the Alid page says 'The Samanids captured Tabaristan, and the Alavids fled to Daylam in exile (900-913)'. The shape for 901-910 should be Samanid land, not Zaydi (Cliopatria's 898-910 Zaydi row and its 911-921 Samanid row cover the exile years in a muddled way).

correction.text: the 922-925 shape: Tabaristan with the Rayy edge, restored by Hasan al-Utrush in 914

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 914-921, which Cliopatria gives to the Samanids: 'Hasan managed to inflict a crushing defeat upon it in December 913 at Burdidah' and 'was soon able to extend his control over all the old Zaydid domains, including both Tabaristan and Gurgan'; reign from January 914. The Nasr II page adds 'Ray and Tabaristan were taken by the Zaydi Alid Hasan al-Utrush' (no year), so the 922 shape (with the Rayy edge) is used.

40.6 thousand km2, the restored state under Hasan ibn al-Qasim (deposed 923-926 by the Nasiris) to the Samanid conquest of 928. The Nasr II page: Asfar ibn Shiruya 'conquered Tabaristan and Ray' in 928.

Holds 926-928 only. The Alid page: 'Disestablished: 928'; the Samanid general Asfar took Tabaristan and Ray in 928, Makan ibn Kaki seized Tabaristan and Gurgan in 930 and was gone by 931, and the Ziyarid Mardavij held them from about 932. The Cliopatria row's 929-935 years are not Zaydi land.

ledger.note: 864: Hasan ibn Zayd founds the Zaydi emirate in Tabaristan. 'The first and most powerful Zaydi emirate was established in Tabaristan in 864 and lasted until 928'; 'a rebellion broke out in the towns of Ruyan, Kalar and Chalus' and Hasan 'was recognized as emir by a part of the local population' (Hasan ibn Zayd page).
865: Hasan is driven out of Tabaristan. 'he was chased out of Tabaristan in 865 by Sulayman ibn Abdallah' (the Tahirid dossier has him recovering it the same year).

865: Hasan is back in Tabaristan the same year. 'he was chased out of Tabaristan in 865 by Sulayman ibn Abdallah, but returned within the same year' and 'recovered the province' (year and confidence corrected by the me-08-b reviewer from 866, c1).
867: Hasan holds Gurgan. 'Exploiting the turmoils of the period, from 867 Hasan also usually controlled Gurgan to the east.'
874: Ya'qub al-Saffar invades Tabaristan. 'Ya'qub invaded Tabaristan and defeated the Zaydid forces at Sari', forcing Hasan 'once again to flee to the mountains of Daylam'.
874: the Saffarid army, 'hurt by heavy rain and disease', withdraws shortly after; the page does not say when Hasan came back from Daylam.
Spring 877: Gurgan is lost. 'The Zaydids were expelled from Gurgan by the Tahirid general Ishaq al-Sari in spring 877.'

region.text: most of the Zaydid domains: Tabaristan with the Amul plain

ledger.note: 889: Rafi' ibn Harthama overruns the Zaydid domains. 'the invasion of Rafi' ibn Harthama in 889-892, which occupied most of his domains'; 'Rafi' launched a major invasion of the Zaydid domains and conquered most of them' (888 or 889). The page adds that Muhammad 'gained the support of Justan ibn Vahsudan, lord of Daylam' (888 or 889 period).
24 June 893: Muhammad re-enters Amul. 'Muhammad re-entered Amul on 24 June 893.'
c. 896: Gurgan is recovered. 'Rafi' was killed shortly after by his rivals the Saffarids, whereupon Muhammad recovered Gurgan as well' (the Amr page puts Rafi's death in Khwarazm in 896).
900: Isma'il Samani invades. 'Ismail decided to take advantage of the caliph's grant by sending an army to Tabaristan'; 'The Samanids now demanded the cession of Gurgan'.

3 October 900: Muhammad ibn Zayd dies and the Samanids take Tabaristan. 'the Samanids prevailed, and the severely wounded Muhammad was captured'; 'He died on the next day, 3 October 900'; 'the Samanids took over the province'. The Alavids fled to Daylam in exile (900-913).
October 900: the fighting ends with the Samanid victory at Gurgan.
December 913: al-Utrush returns. 'Hasan managed to inflict a crushing defeat upon it in December 913 at Burdidah on the river Burrud west of Chalus' (the Samanid army sent under Muhammad ibn Sa'luk).
914: the Samanids, whose amir Ahmad was murdered in January 914, leave Tabaristan to al-Utrush ('Taking advantage of the murder of Ahmad ibn Ismai'il soon after').

Rayy under al-Utrush. The Nasr II page says 'Ray and Tabaristan were taken by the Zaydi Alid Hasan al-Utrush' without a year; the al-Utrush page has Rayy only as his refuge in 900. The year is bridged from his reign start.

January 914: Hasan al-Utrush restores the Zaydi emirate. 'Reign: January 914 - January/February 917'; 'Hasan was soon able to extend his control over all the old Zaydid domains, including both Tabaristan and Gurgan'; the Alid page says restored 'in 914 by another Alid branch'.

928: the Samanids end the Zaydi state. 'In 928, Asfar ibn Shiruya, a Dailamite military leader who now served the Samanids, conquered Tabaristan and Ray'; the Alid page: 'Disestablished: 928'; Hasan ibn al-Qasim died that year.
928: the Zaydi emirate of Tabaristan ends under the second Samanid conquest. 'Local Zaydi rulers survived in Daylam and Gilan until the 16th century.'

wars.name: Zaydi–Tahirid war over Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Hasan chased out in 865 by Sulayman ibn Abdallah, back in Tabaristan by 867 and usually in control of Gurgan from 867.
wars.note: Hasan was forced into Daylam again by the Abbasid general Muflih in 869; no territorial change recorded.

wars.name: Saffarid invasion of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Ya'qub beat the Zaydid forces at Sari; his army withdrew shortly after, hurt by rain and disease.

wars.name: Zaydi–Abbasid wars of Hasan ibn Zayd
wars.outcome: Rayy changed hands repeatedly (864-865, 867, 870 and 872 under Hasan); Muhammad ibn Zayd failed to take it from Asategin in August 885; Gurgan lost in spring 877.

wars.name: Rafi' ibn Harthama's invasion of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Rafi' occupied most of the Zaydid domains 889-892; Muhammad re-entered Amul on 24 June 893 and recovered Gurgan after Rafi's death.

wars.name: Samanid conquest of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Samanid victory near Gurgan; Muhammad ibn Zayd died on 3 October 900; Alids in exile in Daylam 900-913.

wars.name: Zaydi restoration under al-Utrush
wars.outcome: Crushing defeat of the Samanid army at Burdidah in December 913; Tabaristan and Gurgan recovered in 914.

wars.name: Samanid reconquest of Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Asfar ibn Shiruya took Tabaristan and Ray in 928, ending the state.

certainty.note: Mountain and forest frontiers of Tabaristan, Daylam and Gilan; Rayy, Gurgan and Qazvin changed hands repeatedly and are only ever approximate.

sources.title: Alid dynasties of northern Iran
sources.note: Dates 864-928, capital Amol, the 900-913 interregnum, 914 restoration, rulers.

sources.note: 864 foundation, 865 expulsion, Gurgan 867, Rayy and Qazvin episodes, Saffarid invasion 874.

notes: Cliopatria's Zaydi row (866..935, with gaps 892-895 and 911-921) is partly muddled: the state began in 864 and ended in 928; the Samanids held Tabaristan 900-913 (Alid page: 'in exile (900-913)'); Rafi' ibn Harthama, not the Samanids, took most of the domains in 889-893, so Cliopatria's 892-895 gap is really 889-June 893. No Alid page opened gives an area, so no area comparison was possible (the shape is about 41 thousand km2, roughly Tabaristan plus the Gilan edge). Pages disagree on the Hasan ibn Zayd's expulsion (865 Hasan page vs. recovery 'that same year' in the Tahirid dossier), on Muhammad's death (3 October 900 on his page; the Samanid page's 901 for the Ray campaign) and on Rayy (Nasr II page has al-Utrush taking it; the al-Utrush page has only his flight there). Rayy, Qumis, Qazvin and Gilan are temporary holdings and only the Rayy edge is in the 914 and 922 shapes. Counterparts without a dossier: Rafi' ibn Harthama (a warlord of Khorasan, 888-896, who held most of Tabaristan 889-893) needs a dossier or an entry in a Khorasan batch; the Justanids of Daylam and the Asfar/Makan Daylamite commanders (928-931) are also missing; Natural Earth has no Gurgan admin-1 (Golestan is the modern province), so Gorgan 80 km is used. Not opened (page budget 5; four used for this state alone): Hasan ibn al-Qasim, Makan ibn Kaki, Justanids, Battle of Burdidah.
